$comment: Single source of truth for the Message API. Every framework package is tested against this file.
name: message
title: Message
description: One chat message: who wrote it and when, the content, and small icon actions such as copy, retry and thumbs up or down.
thumb:

Cache your modules and run tests in parallel.

avatar.description: Usually an Avatar. Hidden from screen readers, because the author name says who it is.

time / dateTime.description: The time to show, and the machine-readable time (then it is a <time> element).

align.description: "end" puts the avatar on the end side, for the person's own messages.

streaming.description: The reply is still being written: a caret after the text, and aria-busy so screen readers wait.

MessageAction.description: A small icon button with a label (its aria-label). pressed makes it a toggle.

MessageCopy.description: Copies the content (or text) and says "Copied" for two seconds.
MessageCopy.html: the button with data-vin-copy (vinui.js; add data-vin-message to the article)

MessageFeedback.description: Thumbs up and down; one at a time. value, defaultValue, onValueChange ("up" | "down" | null).
MessageFeedback.html: buttons with data-vin-feedback="up|down" and aria-pressed (vinui.js); listen for the vin-feedback event

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: An assistant message with copy, retry and thumbs up or down. In HTML, add data-vin-message to the article so copy and feedback work.

examples.title: Conversation
examples.description: The person's message on the end side in a Bubble, and a reply they liked.

examples.title: Streaming
examples.description: While the reply is written: a caret after the text and aria-busy. Add the actions when it's done.

a11y: Each message is an <article>; the author and a <time> element come first, so screen readers say who and when before the content.
The avatar is hidden from screen readers because the author name already says who it is.
Actions are a labelled group of buttons. Every icon button has a label, and the thumbs use aria-pressed so their state is read out.
Actions are always visible, not only on hover, so they work with touch and the keyboard.
While a reply streams, aria-busy="true" asks screen readers to wait until it is finished. The caret stops blinking when motion is reduced.
